sections.content: Talking about learning experiences requires control of the main past tenses. The imperfecto gives background and habitual context, while the indefinido presents completed events. The present can connect a past experience to the learner's current situation.

items.spanish: Cuando era estudiante, estudiaba mucho antes de los exámenes.
items.english: When I was a student, I used to study a lot before exams.

items.spanish: El año pasado aprobé una asignatura difícil.
items.english: Last year I passed a difficult subject.

items.spanish: Antes me costaba concentrarme, pero ahora estudio con más facilidad.
items.english: I used to find it difficult to concentrate, but now I study more easily.

sections.content: Use the imperfecto for background and habitual past situations, the indefinido for completed events, and the present for the current result or situation.
